movie.title: The Mortuary Assistant
movie.overview: Rebecca Owens, a recent mortuary science graduate takes a night shift job at River Fields Mortuary. Initially, the job seems straightforward — embalming bodies, completing paperwork, and keeping things tidy. But once Rebecca starts working the night shift, things take a dark turn.

reviews.author: graeaehorror
reviews.content:
Everything is here to make this a great horror – a creepy setting, extensive backstory, a strong fan following, but something doesn’t quite hit right. Instead of playing to these strengths, the film leans more into horror tropes (jump scares, a lightening storm that strikes at the exact right moments, creepy pasta looking cg creatures).

This really is a film for fans of the game. If like myself you've not played it, this adaptation feels like a rushed effort full of weird graphic choices and plot devices. It could do with time dedicated to giving everyone an opportunity to immerse in its world and enjoy the carnage that lies ahead.

There's a lot of puzzle based moments, reminiscent of an escape room experience which again plays well in the realm of RPGs. Throw in confusing time loops and flashbacks without much exposition and it leaves air for confusion to creep in. You spend more time trying to trace the missing puzzle pieces of story together than being able to let the narrative unfold as it should.

Some scenes have an odd looking visual style. The foreground is fine, but the background feels all digital and comes across as cheap looking on film. After the screening I checked out streams of the gameplay and it's clear to see now when compared this is a replication of the look and feel. They're trying to immerse those fans into an expended universe which is great except it doesn't do the film any justice.

Ultimately I feel The Mortuary Assistant falls into the same traps as many video game adaptations. Trying to replicate the exact style, feel and gameplay does not work. It needs to feel like you're on a journey with the characters, not wanting to reach through the screen and guide them through impossible logic, puzzle set pieces and unfathomable plot. Silent Hill is a grade A example of this - a huge fan base that's let down by the over ambition to cover everything in a franchise in one feature film and loses its audience completely.

All that aside, there are a elements I like, mostly the practical effects. We have oozing wounds, corpses with their guts out and pus for everyone which are always shining moments for independent filmmaking. There's some great foley work and sound design too, with a memorable moment of a jaw grinding and cracking as they open it to insert the embalming tube which made me gag!

If you liked The Mortuary Assistant game this will be for you. But for those without that experience, proceed with an open mind. Much like Iron Lung, these adaptations won't be for everyone. On the upside, I definitely want to play the game now!

reviews.author: Gordon
reviews.content:
I had huge hope for this movie as the trailer is outstanding. 
It seems that about 40 minutes into the film there is what I would consider to be a significant time jump. 
You go from the natural progression of the story to jumping straight into the meat and bones of a possession story.

It had such promise.

reviews.author: Sierbahnn
reviews.content: The game is better. This is not as engaging as the Autopsy of Jane Doe, or even other game-adaptations like Exit 8 or Iron Lung. This is more like Five Nights at Freddy's where they try to tack on bits of lore as story and character, and it just comes out flat. And this movie is trying to set up the plot to enjoy a sequel, too. Shame they didn't make the movie itself more interesting. The casting and directing is good enough, the effects are standard, but the plot, writing, the narrative structure, just leaves this feeling dry and boring.

reviews.author: Dean
reviews.content: It's average at best. The only thing I liked in this movie the pretty actress, that's it. What I didn't like most was shifting from reality into unreality where it gets harder to understand what's reality and what's not. It wasn't that bad, but it wasn't good idea. I think 5/10 is the suitable rating for this movie.

aiEnrichment.summary_one_sentence: A newly qualified mortuary assistant working a night shift at River Fields Mortuary discovers the premises are haunted by a lethal demonic entity she must identify and banish to survive.
aiEnrichment.summary_short: Rebecca Owens begins a late-night shift at River Fields Mortuary expecting a routine evening of embalming and paperwork. However, unexplainable paranormal events quickly escalate as a malevolent demon targets her and begins a terrifying possession process. To save her soul, Rebecca must perform dark rituals, decipher cryptic clues, and correctly identify which corpse harbors the entity before sunrise.
aiEnrichment.summary_long: After finishing her degree in mortuary science, Rebecca Owens accepts a late-night position at River Fields Mortuary under the guidance of the enigmatic mortician, Raymond. What begins as a calm evening of routine embalming rapidly devolves into a nightmare when supernatural phenomena manifest throughout the facility. Rebecca experiences disturbing hallucinations, moving corpses, and erratic shifts in the mortuary's environment. She soon learns that a demonic force has trapped her inside and intends to bind itself to her body. Guided by cassette tapes and hidden notes left behind by Raymond, she learns she must perform a specific exorcism ritual. To succeed, she must gather reagents, identify the demon's sigils, and determine which of the three bodies in the cold room harbors the entity. As the night progresses, the demon uses Rebecca's traumatic past and struggles with addiction against her to break her mental resolve. Pushed to the brink of insanity, Rebecca fights through grueling hallucinations to complete the embalmings and apply the correct sigil-marked talisman. Ultimately, her accuracy in identifying the demon dictates whether she escapes the shift alive or becomes permanently possessed.
aiEnrichment.synopsis: Rebecca Owens, a recent graduate in mortuary science, takes on a night shift at the secluded River Fields Mortuary to gain hands-on experience under veteran mortician Raymond. Expecting an evening dedicated solely to embalming, body preparation, and administrative duties, Rebecca is instead thrust into a terrifying supernatural ordeal. As strange occurrences escalate into outright demonic manifestations, she uncovers the mortuary's dark secret: it frequently acts as a battleground against demonic entities seeking human hosts. trapped inside, Rebecca must learn the intricate, dark mechanics of identifying and binding a demon while maintaining her sanity and performing her standard duties. The atmospheric mystery blends body horror with a race against time, forcing Rebecca to confront both her personal trauma and an ancient evil before her night shift ends.

story_structure.climax: With her sanity pushed to the limit, Rebecca prepares the final sigils and ritual elements to burn the correct possessed body before the demon fully consumes her soul.
story_structure.conflict: Strange, unsettling paranormal phenomena begin occurring throughout the facility, trapping Rebecca inside and forcing her to realize she is being targeted by a demonic force.
story_structure.resolution: Rebecca either survives the ordeal and successfully banishes the entity—continuing her harrowing work at River Fields—or succumbs to possession, depending on the accuracy of her ritual choices.
story_structure.introduction: Rebecca Owens, a recent mortuary science graduate, arrives for a night shift at River Fields Mortuary to perform routine embalming tasks and administrative work.
story_structure.risingAction: As supernatural disturbances escalate, Rebecca must balance her terrifying surroundings with performing precise mortuary procedures to identify the specific demon and the exact body it has possessed before her time runs out.

faq.answer: The Mortuary Assistant is primarily a supernatural horror film, featuring strong elements of psychological thriller and demonic lore.
faq.question: What is the dominant genre of The Mortuary Assistant?

faq.answer: Yes, the movie is a feature film adaptation of the popular 2022 indie horror video game of the same name developed by DarkStone Digital.
faq.question: Is this film based on a video game?

faq.answer: The story follows Rebecca Owens, a recent mortuary science graduate who takes a night shift at River Fields Mortuary, only to uncover demonic forces tied to the corpses she is preparing.
faq.question: What is the basic premise of the story?

faq.answer: No, it is currently a standalone film adaptation, though its origins stem from the interactive video game universe.
faq.question: Is this movie part of a cinematic franchise?

faq.answer: The majority of the narrative takes place inside the claustrophobic and unsettling setting of River Fields Mortuary during a single overnight shift.
faq.question: Where does most of the film take place?

faq.answer: No, there is no post-credits scene, but the ending leaves lasting psychological implications for the main character.
faq.question: Is there a post-credits scene?

faq.answer: The main protagonist is Rebecca Owens, a young woman attempting to rebuild her life while facing terrifying supernatural events at her new job.
faq.question: Who is the main protagonist of the story?

faq.answer: The film explores themes of trauma, guilt, addiction recovery, mortality, and personal demonology intermingled with supernatural horrors.
faq.question: What key themes are explored in the narrative?

faq.answer: It relies heavily on both, combining sudden eerie occurrences and body horror during embalming tasks with persistent psychological dread.
faq.question: Does the movie feature jump scares or psychological dread?

faq.answer: The primary threat comes from an insidious demonic entity that possesses one of the bodies in the mortuary and attempts to bind itself to Rebecca.
faq.question: Who is the primary antagonist in the film?
